confidence_rationale: Canonical review by the group that defined the reality-filtering paradigm, synthesising two decades of patient and electrophysiological work. It is strong, well-replicated evidence that a dedicated pre-commitment gate EXISTS -- a distinct faculty that decides whether an evoked memory 'refers to the present and can be acted upon' -- which is precisely MECH-037's functional posit, and the failure phenotype (confabulation acted upon, plus disorientation) is exactly the failure MECH-037 predicts. Direction is mixed rather than supports because the review locates the gate's decision mechanism in orbitofrontal extinction capacity and reward-system structures, NOT in hippocampal trace strength or temporal-ordering support. MECH-037 as currently written routes the gate through a hippocampal trace / temporal-ordering signal; the best-developed human account of this same function routes it elsewhere. Source quality is high but it is a narrative review, not primary data, so confidence is held below the 0.8 band.
failure_signatures: Confabulating patients act upon evoked memories that no longer relate to the present, while item recognition and general memory capacity can be comparatively spared -- so a gate keyed only on trace STRENGTH would not produce this phenotype.
Disorientation and confabulation co-occur and recover together, indicating a single gating faculty rather than a byproduct of graded memory degradation.

The locus of the critical lesion is posterior medial orbitofrontal cortex / basal forebrain, not hippocampus -- a REE implementation that made the hippocampal trace signal the sole gate variable would have no analogue of the human lesion that actually abolishes the function.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Studies of patients who confuse reality (confabulation, disorientation) indicate that the brain determines whether an evoked memory refers to the present -- and may therefore be acted upon -- by recruiting a phylogenetically old orbitofrontal faculty, extinction, together with reward-system structures. Failure of this filter, not failure of memory storage, is what produces behaviourally enacted confabulation.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the closest human-neuroscience analogue of MECH-037's core posit: a filtering stage sits between retrieved/generated candidate content and the decision to commit and act on it, and the filter is dissociable from the content it filters. In REE terms, that is exactly a gate between E1-generated candidates and E3 commitment licensing, and the reviewed phenotype confirms that degrading the gate yields high-confidence commitment of ungrounded content -- MECH-037's stated confirming signature. What it does NOT support is MECH-037's choice of gating VARIABLE. The review's mechanism is orbitofrontal extinction: suppressing memory traces that no longer have current reward/behavioural relevance. That is a relevance/valence computation, not a trace-presence or temporal-ordering computation. If REE keeps MECH-037 as stated, the substrate should probably carry BOTH inputs -- trace/ordering support AND an extinction-like relevance suppressor -- and an experiment should be able to tell which one is doing the gating work.
mapping.mapping_caveat: A narrative review, so the evidence is summarised rather than presented; effect sizes and individual study designs must be taken from the primary papers. The human 'reality filter' is defined operationally by a continuous recognition task, which is a far narrower construct than REE's general provenance gate over arbitrary E1 content. Most critically, the transfer assumed here -- that REE's Papez-like loop is the right analogue for a function the review attributes to orbitofrontal cortex and the reward system -- is the very thing in question; treating this paper as confirmation of the Papez routing would be circular.
mapping.source_context: Human clinical neuropsychology and evoked-potential work; confabulating and disoriented patients versus controls, continuous recognition paradigm.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (canonical review, well-replicated paradigm, human data). Mapping fidelity is the limiting term: the paper's construct maps well onto 'pre-commitment gate' but poorly onto 'hippocampal trace / temporal-ordering signal as the gating variable'. Transfer risk moderate -- the construct is human and behavioural, and REE's generalisation from a recognition-task filter to a general provenance gate is untested.
